engine.note: Cloned read-only; driven externally. Not modified by this harness.

scenarios.name: Leader killed mid-write
scenarios.description: A write is proposed and the leader is crashed in the same tick, before replication completes. Acknowledged writes must survive; the in-flight one is permitted to vanish.
scenarios.fault_summary: NodeCrash on the current leader, one tick after a proposal

scenarios.name: Network partition, two groups
scenarios.description: The cluster splits into a one-node minority holding the old leader and a four-node majority. The majority must elect a new leader and keep committing. A write aimed at the isolated leader must never commit, and must not survive the partition healing.
scenarios.fault_summary: Partition: {old leader} | rest of cluster, healed after 150 ticks

detail.note: uncommitted entry overwritten before ack (correct behaviour)

scenarios.name: Delayed and dropped links
scenarios.description: Two specific links are degraded while writes continue: one gains six ticks of latency, the other drops half its messages. Consensus must still converge and every acknowledged write must survive.
scenarios.fault_summary: LinkFault n1<->n3 delay 6 ticks; LinkFault n2<->n4 drop 50%

scenarios.name: Repeated elections under write load
scenarios.description: Whoever holds leadership is isolated and released four times in a row while writes keep arriving, forcing repeated elections. Term numbers should climb steadily and no acknowledged write may be lost across any leadership handover.
scenarios.fault_summary: Four successive Partition faults, each isolating the sitting leader

scenarios.name: Crash during an active partition
scenarios.description: A node is crashed inside the majority side while the network is already split, taking the reachable set to exactly a bare quorum. Both faults are then healed together.
scenarios.fault_summary: Partition {leader} | rest, then NodeCrash inside the majority, both healed

scenarios.name: Quorum loss and recovery
scenarios.description: Three of five nodes are crashed, making a quorum impossible. A write issued during that window must NOT be acknowledged while it lasts -- it may only commit once enough nodes return. Unavailability here is correct behaviour, not a failure; the timeline below shows the write sitting unacknowledged until the restarts land.
scenarios.fault_summary: Three sequential NodeCrash faults, then all three restarted
